html:
A beer festival held every autumn in Munich, the capital of Bavaria. It began in 1810 and is now the largest folk festival in the world, with several million visitors each year.

The first one celebrated the wedding of Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria, later King Ludwig I, and Princess Therese of Saxe Hildburghausen on 12 October 1810. The people of Munich were invited to a horse race in a meadow outside the city, which was named the Theresienwiese after the bride. The race was repeated the next year, and over time fairground rides, food stalls and beer tents were added.

The festival now starts in September and ends in the first days of October. Only beer from Munich's own big breweries can be served, in great halls holding thousands. It is cancelled only for war and epidemics. Its image of dirndls, lederhosen and litre mugs has been copied by Oktoberfests around the world, which spread with German emigrants.
